story_text.value:
Been working on this for almost two years now and want to ask for feedback here.

Started from the wish to have an open-source, privacy focused medication tracker, where at the time being none existed. So I created one myself.

Core features are:

- Fully offline (does not even have permission to access the net)

- Unlimited medications and reminders

- Various reminder types (daily at a certain time, interval, daily intervals etc.)

- Highly configurable reminder engine (repeating reminders, reminders as alarms, snoozing)

- Medication stock tracking with configurable alarms for stock thresholds and expiration date

- Medication intake is logged and can be exported as PDF or CSV

I started with Java and XML, but have gradually shifted to using (and learning) Kotlin. Compose is on my to-learn-and-do-list for this year.

story_text.value:
Hi HN, we built Prizmi because we wanted an AI assistant that would i) do real and interesting things instead of explaining how to do them ourselves, ii) act on all our devices, iii) be proactive in true sense, iv) keep us in full control, v) respect our privacy, vi) be easy to set up, and vii) be used by non-technical people including seniors. This is what Prizmi is designed to do: you text it from a messaging app, and it acts for you across your phone and your computers. It's also proactive, so you can set something up once and it keeps running. It also follows up on its own when it has something useful to say.

Some examples:

- "Check my email every weekday at 9am, 11am, 3pm, and 5pm and draft replies for me"

- "Send me a reminder to take my medication every day at 6pm"

- "Look at my screen and solve this coding question"

- "Sort my Downloads folder by file type"

- "Turn on my gmail vacation auto-reply from monday to friday, and write a message for me."

It remembers what you've told it, so if it decides to check-in with you, it would be specific not generic. You can turn check-ins and any other skills on or off with one toggle.

Your chat history and what Prizmi remembers are encrypted and each person's data is kept separate. Prizmi does not click Submit, Pay, or Send; you are the one who makes the final call.

We are bootstrapped. If you can, please give it a try at prizmi.ai (there are demo videos on the homepage and you'll have some free credits to get started). We are specifically looking for feedback on onboarding, things that confused you or you think would be confusing for a non-technical user, tasks that you tried but it couldn't handle, or any feature or skills that you think we should build. Happy to answer questions. Thank you!

story_text.value:
Some friends and I built RingReminder over a few nights / weekends as a side project - the core problem we were trying to solve was "how can we improve the reliability of our friends/family, so they do the things they are supposed to?", like show up to social plans on time, take their medications, etc...

The solution we landed on was a telephone-based automated reminder service - controlled from your calendar app.

The hypothesis driving our solution was while many people may check their email every few seconds / view upcoming events in their calendars, everyone we know picks up calls to their phones. Therefore, if we could create a near-frictionless method of automatically calling our friends to remind them to leave early, maybe we could improve their reliability. The calendar seemed like a natural place to do this - Just invite a ringreminder.com email address to the calendar entry, and a telephone call reminder is set. Also, us organized folks already used our calendar apps to keep track of when we were meeting said friends.

On the back end, its built in Java (spring framework) - we basically poll a mail account at regular intervals checking for calendar invites (Google/iCal or Outlook format) - we then parse out the necessary information to schedule the reminder call from the invite, and call Twilio to make the outgoing call. Any changes to the event (including cancellation) are automatically processed, assuming that you let your calendar app notify all guests to the event of the change. There is also a web CRUD interface for manually managing reminders.

Let me know if you have any questions!

title.value: Show HN: Schedule phone call reminders from within your favorite calendar app -

story_text.value:
I built a smart online medication cabinet that helps you organize and manage your home medications. AppaMed is a web application designed to address the common problem of medication management, especially for those dealing with multiple prescriptions or caring for family members.

Key features: - Intelligent medication tracking with expiration dates and quantity management - Smart reminders for dosage schedules - Proactive expiry alerts to prevent usage of outdated medications

Tech stack: - Next.js 13 with App Router - TypeScript - Tailwind CSS for styling - Shadcn UI for component library - PostgreSQL

The project aims to leverage modern web technologies to improve medication adherence and reduce the risks associated with improper medication management. It follows best practices for accessibility and responsive design to ensure a seamless user experience across devices.

I'm particularly interested in feedback on: 1. Additional smart features that could enhance medication management 2. Suggestions for improving data privacy and security in health-related applications 3. Ideas for integrating with health tracking devices or APIs to make the cabinet even smarter

I'd love to hear your thoughts and suggestions on how to make this smart medication cabinet even more intelligent and user-friendly!

story_text.value:
Hey HN,

I’m Aliaksei Saskevich, CTO & Software Engineer at Sequoia Health. My team and I have built an iOS app to help men improve their sexual health through lifestyle changes and guided exercises — no medications involved.

We noticed that many men struggle to talk about sexual health and often seek help only when things get critical. Our goal is to offer a science-backed, stigma-free tool that helps earlier and more effectively.

What makes Sequoia different:

- Exercises are personalized based on the IIEF test (International Index of Erectile Function).

- Content is written by certified sexologists and psychologists on our team.

- We offer optional online consultations with real specialists.

- We’re building a structured knowledge base focused on practical, non-pharmaceutical solutions.

Achievements so far:

- Partnered with a local lab to offer discounts to users.

- Members of the World Association of Sexologists.

- Official partners of UNFPA.

- Ranked #2 and #5 Product of the Day on Product Hunt: https://www.producthunt.com/products/sequoia-men-s-sexual-we....

Results:

- We ran a user survey inside the app — 79% of respondents reported improvements in their sexual health. Full report: https://sequoia.health/research/research-report-user-survey-...

- The study was accepted and presented at a medical conference.

Current features:

- 21-day exercise plan with progressive difficulty

- Symptom tracker

- Articles by medical professionals

- Calendar & reminders

- Regular checkups

- Health stats dashboard

What we’re working on now:

- AI-driven personalization: We’re developing an AI module that analyzes user input and IIEF results to recommend tailored exercise plans and summarize the user’s current health status in clear, actionable terms.

- Integrated online consultations: Users can now book sessions directly with certified sexologists and psychologists through the app — for deeper guidance, emotional support, or clarification on their progress.

Pricing:

- Limited free features

- Monthly: $19.99

- 3 Months: $38.99

- Annual: $69.99

- Lifetime: $199.99

Would love feedback on:

- UI/UX: What works, what doesn’t?

- Features: What feels essential, missing, or over-complicated?

- Pricing: Does it feel fair for what’s offered?

- Motivation: What drives users to pay for health apps like this?

Try it here: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id1553925344

We’re iOS-only for now and actively looking for an Android developer to help us expand.

Thanks for reading — happy to answer any questions or dive deeper into the tech, research, or product decisions.

I’m excited to introduce Panda Meditation Timer, a minimalist, distraction free timer designed to help you focus on your meditation practice.

After struggling with overly complicated meditation apps that added unnecessary features, I decided to create Panda, a simple tool that helps you set your meditation session with ease and stay present during your practice. It’s all about simplicity and mindfulness, without the clutter.

Panda is perfect for beginners and experienced who want a tool that helps them focus on their practice, not on setting up complex apps.

story_text.value:
I started this project by running 10-day group challenges on Whatsapp. The group was gathered via a Webflow landing page, Google forms, Zapier and a PayPal button (here’s what I posted on HN at that time - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=32363731).

The WhatsApp challenges turned out to be a hit with over 85% checking in daily and 45% repaying to join multiple challenges.

After having tried Streaks, Habitify, GTD, reminder apps, google calendar, Notion...etc—I was still having trouble staying consistent with my personal/wellness goals and habits. Methods from Atomic Habits by James Clear—are what worked best for me—but sticking to it alone was hard. For example, I had a daily push-up reminder on my google calendar that I ignored for almost a year.

Fast forward, I’m now on day 120+ doing push-ups, meditation and waking up before 6am—after participating in group accountability challenges :)

To see if we can scale it to help more people and potentially build a community-driven business—we just released an iOS app.

Recap of how it works:

- Join 10-30 day accountability challenges in small groups of 3-12 people

- Commit a daily goal and check-in with the group on whether you didn’t or didn’t do it

- Daily visual progress reports, reward credits/penalties and support from others helps everyone stay on track

- Create and join private challenges with friends

Would love to have you try it by joining a challenge—and see if could help you become the person you want be for 2023!

story_text.value:
Hi all,

I just made this Chrome extension I would like to hear your feedback on:

http://alexisrondeau.com/reup/

The extension will ask you to define a goal while working within Chrome. Once you've set yourself that goal it will be visible on any webpage you visit after that.

Some background: I've been noticing how much time I tend to waste online, especially Facebook, HackerNews, and tried many different ways to control the habit.

There are extensions and methods out there that should help with this kind of behavior, for example StayFocusd or LeechBlock, but I have found myself not being able to stay on track even with them. After a while I wind up just using a different browser. Please note, this is not a shortcoming of the extensions, but of my own self-control.

So, instead of blocking sites, I thought it good to stay reminded of what I set out to do in the first place (For example: "Finish todays project and deploy", "Get inspired", "Research meditation techniques"). Usually, when I know what I want, the internet is an amazing tool. If I forget about it, things just get messy and wasteful...

If you are interested, give it a spin. Any feedback or questions are highly appreciated.

In best case I would like to know how it does -- or doesn't -- affect your productivity positively over the course of several days and if there is a breakingpoint of annoyance over time.

title.value: Show HN: A Chrome extension for goal-based browsing

story_text.value:
October 29th Update

What's new, in 10 seconds.

* iMessage & SMS actions: have Praxos read incoming messages and do tasks for you. * Message search: Search across all your text conversations and contacts. * Quality of life upgrades: video and image editing, location-based actions, file retrieval, and more.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

iMessage & SMS actions

Praxos can auto-forward inbound iMessages and SMS messages.

This means that you can have your conversations stored, and later used to set up triggers or automatic actions based on the contents of incoming messages.

You have granular over this feature, from picking specific senders to only taking action based on wording. It can also be much more general.

For example:

* If I receive a message from my dad asking me to buy milk on my way home, add it to my shopping list. * If Lucas asks me to edit a document he is drafting before Nov. 1st, add a deadline to my Google Calendar, attach the file to the event, and remind me about it next Saturday morning. * If Praxos texts my grandmother to take her medication, and she does not respond, ping me before end of day. * If I receive promotional messages, automatically reply stop. * If my mom asks me to send receipts of my last purchase, automatically fetch the receipt from my email and send it to her.

Forwarding messages means that you can now also search across your entire conversation history!

If you would like to start adding these automations, connect with us on Discord ( https://discord.gg/wVmrXD2dJA ) and we will help you one-on-one. They require special setup; we are working on simplifying the process.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quality of life upgrades

* Location based functionalities: Praxos can now find stuff near you, using the location to find products, paths, restaurants, etc. * Extended webhooks: We now support webhook triggers for Outlook as well. Calendar/Drive will soon be added. * Editing Images and Videos is now possible. * Voice note support: send Praxos a voice note with what you want done, and it'll get done. It works the same as text! * Messaging systems are more robust. Praxos will ask you to clarify your message if something is missing or ambiguous. * File retrieval upgrade: Praxos can now find old files that you have uploaded directly, and even fetch them for you on command/send them to you as needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Curious to give it a try? Visit us at https://mypraxos.com.

You have granular over this feature, from picking specific senders to only taking action based on wording. It can also be much more general.

For example:

* If I receive a message from my dad asking me to buy milk on my way home, add it to my shopping list. * If Lucas asks me to edit a document he is drafting before Nov. 1st, add a deadline to my Google Calendar, attach the file to the event, and remind me about it next Saturday morning. * If Praxos texts my grandmother to take her medication, and she does not respond, ping me before end of day. * If I receive promotional messages, automatically reply stop. * If my mom asks me to send receipts of my last purchase, automatically fetch the receipt from my email and send it to her.

Forwarding messages means that you can now also search across your entire conversation history!

If you would like to start adding these automations, connect with us on Discord ( https://discord.gg/wVmrXD2dJA ) and we will help you one-on-one. They require special setup; we are working on simplifying the process.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quality of life upgrades

* Location based functionalities: Praxos can now find stuff near you, using the location to find products, paths, restaurants, etc. * Extended webhooks: We now support webhook triggers for Outlook as well. Calendar/Drive will soon be added. * Editing Images and Videos is now possible. * Voice note support: send Praxos a voice note with what you want done, and it'll get done. It works the same as text! * Messaging systems are more robust. Praxos will ask you to clarify your message if something is missing or ambiguous. * File retrieval upgrade: Praxos can now find old files that you have uploaded directly, and even fetch them for you on command/send them to you as needed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Curious to give it a try? Visit us at https://mypraxos.com.

Over the past year, I’ve been building a deeply personal project called Eiren AI — a mindfulness and growth app designed to help people reduce overwhelm, stay grounded, and make daily progress toward their goals.

It's built on a simple but powerful idea: What if your personal growth app could think with you? Not just track tasks, but also support your emotions, help you journal, and generate meditations based on how you feel?

Eiren AI helps users: -Turn visions into structured goals and daily tasks with AI support. -Reflect through journaling (with templates + AI autocomplete). -Generate personalized meditations based on current mental or emotional states. -Get guidance via a calm and friendly in-app AI chat.

I’m launching officially on May 9, but the landing page is live now. You can get reminded at launch when you sign up to the newsletter at https://eiren.ai/newsletter. I'm currently focusing on feedback, early user interviews, and ensuring the experience is smooth across platforms.

Tech stack: -Built with FlutterFlow -Firebase + Firestore backend -GPT via OpenAI (for journaling/vision gen) -ElevenLabs (for meditation voiceovers) -RevenueCat for subscriptions

The app follows a freemium model, with most features unlocked in a CHF 19/month plan (~$20) or a yearly plan for 99.- (around 8.- / month).

If this resonates with you — whether you're into AI, habit-building, mental clarity, or building tools that feel good to use — I’d love your feedback. Especially on the landing page, onboarding clarity, and app concept overall.

https://eiren.ai

Thanks for reading, and much love to everyone here building things that matter.

– Tobias

story_text.value:
Hey everyone! After running a public beta for Zenitizer over the last couple months, it is now officially available to download on the App Store: https://zenitizer.app/install

My goal was to create a clean and simple (yet highly customizable) timer for "unguided meditations" (i.e. no spoken word content).

The timer is customizable with a range of different bells and soothing background soundscapes. Regular interval bells remind the user to return their focus on the breath when thoughts drift off. You can save your favorite timer presets as "routines" and quickly play them via Siri or Home Screen Widgets.

Users are motivated to keep up a regular meditation practice by setting a daily goal and tracking their meditation streak: It is sufficient to meditate even one minute a day to keep the streak - you only need to reach your goal to grow the streak. I wanted to prevent users from feeling pressure about breaking streaks and reward them for meditating at all, however little.

Personally, I am particularly happy about Zenitizer's deep Shortcuts integration. Just say "Hey Siri, meditate with Zenitizer" or "Check my Zenitizer streak". With Shortcuts, you can also build cool automations like starting a meditation, setting a HomeKit scene and enabling Do Not Disturb Focus Mode with a single command.

title.value: Show HN: Zenitizer – Clean and Simple Meditation for Apple Devices

story_text.value:
Hi HN, Gabriel here.

This is a standalone binaural beat generator, combined with a two-deck local audio player built with the Web Audio API.

It includes ten harmonic carrier pairs, seven brainwave-state presets, per-harmonic mixing (so the binaural tones aren't out-of-tune with the music), adjustable beat and carrier frequencies, two oscillator shapes, offline key/BPM analysis, automatic carrier matching, adaptive impulse noise, playlist support, and output recording.

The main problem I've had with existing "binaural beat" generators is that the tone generated does not remain in-tune with what I'm listening to.

This becomes highly noticeable, kind of ruining both the binaural beat and the music ("wrong, Marge, two perfectly good jackets!").

That's the issue this solves, and then I added a bunch of nice-to-haves on top.

It's open-source, free, etc - I'm just sharing because it's something I wanted to exist, and maybe others want it to exist too. Some of you might remember i-Doser, and have - like me - been looking for that same high ever since.

That (urban-legend-coded, totally-trippy-if-you're-fifteen-years-old) app introduced me to "Binaural Beats" - where you play two different tones in each of a person's ears, and the brain scrambles the different frequencies into a single frequency.

As I understand it, this is meant to induce specific brainwaves in the listener, which replicate states like "deep focus" or "half-asleep" or "meditating".

I've not decided personally if this is real science, or new-age pseudoscientific nonsense. It's probably somewhere between the two.

I intentionally haven't looked that hard into studies on the actual effects, because I think placebo is very powerful, and binaural beats work great on me. I find them genuinely useful for focus, meditation, and dream-state creativity. I figure: If it ain't broke, don't learn that it's a placebo. YMMV.

I really love ambient music, and I think that audiobooks could be a much more interesting form if they borrowed more from ideas found in ambient music. That's why I put a second deck on it for spoken-word files. There's some ASMR-y stuff like impulse noise available, also, for those good-good tingles.

I'd like to build it out into a more fully-featured "ambient spoken word" DJ software UI, for making stuff inspired by and adjacent to Glenn Gould's The Idea of North, and I guess this is currently about halfway to that thus far. The playlist function allows you to predefine the binaural tone against tracks playing in the future, so you can set up some pieces of music, and define the brain frequency you are trying to induce (or placebo) in yourself.

I've had a lot of fun putting albums into this, and taking journeys from - for example - "focus" to "deep sleep". I strongly recommend Sea Power's Disco Elysium OST for that, which I've revisited a few times in this software already.

I can't attest to whether the opposite directional journey works, because the "deep sleep" tone has reliably rendered me unconscious.

I hope some of you get some of the same enjoyment (or placebo of enjoyment) I'm getting from it. Feedback, ideas of music that might work well in it, and feature-requests appreciated, especially features in the 'this would make me enjoy using it, but I can't be bothered to add it myself' category.

Edit: I just realised I could have deployed this as a GH Pages page, so you can use it without any setup at all. Doh!

Link to that here - should all work fine in-browser:

https://henrygabriels.github.io/binaural-studio/

title.value: Show HN: Audio Player with "Binaural Beats" tuned to the same key as your music
